findings.title: Tool Poisoning — Hidden Instructions in Tool Descriptions
findings.remediation: Strip or reject tool descriptions containing instruction-override language before registering tools. Apply the same input-validation rules used for user messages.

findings.title: Tool Poisoning — Hidden Instructions in Tool Names
findings.remediation: Enforce an allowlist of safe characters for tool names (e.g. [a-z0-9_\-]{1,64}). Reject names containing whitespace or natural-language sentences.

findings.title: Command Injection — Shell Sequences in Tool Descriptions
findings.owasp_ref: MCP-004: Command Injection via Tool Parameters
findings.remediation: Sanitise all tool descriptions with a strict allowlist before storing or rendering them. Treat them as untrusted user input.

findings.title: Command Injection — Shell Sequences in Tool Input Schemas
findings.owasp_ref: MCP-004: Command Injection via Tool Parameters
findings.remediation: Audit inputSchema default values. Never include executable strings as defaults. Validate schema definitions against a JSON Schema allowlist before publishing.

findings.title: Excessive OAuth Scope — Wildcard File / DB Permissions
findings.owasp_ref: MCP-002: Excessive Permissions & OAuth Scope Abuse
findings.remediation: Replace wildcard scopes with the narrowest scopes needed. For example, replace 'files:*' with 'files:read' if the tool only reads files. Document scope justifications in the manifest.

findings.title: Excessive OAuth Scope — Admin / Full-Access Permissions
findings.owasp_ref: MCP-002: Excessive Permissions & OAuth Scope Abuse
findings.remediation: Never request admin:* or equivalent scopes from an MCP server. Use role-based scopes with explicit resource constraints. Require explicit user consent for any elevated scope.

findings.title: Excessive Agency — Dangerous Tool Names Detected
findings.remediation: Replace generic execution tools with purpose-scoped alternatives (e.g. 'run_sql_query' instead of 'exec'). Apply tool-call allow lists and require human-in-the-loop confirmation for sensitive ops.

findings.title: Sensitive Data Exposure — Credentials Referenced in Tool Descriptions
findings.owasp_ref: MCP-005: Sensitive Data Exposure through Tools
findings.remediation: Remove credential references from tool descriptions. Use opaque parameter names (e.g. 'credential_id') that reference secrets stored in a vault, never inline values.

findings.title: Command Injection Risk — Unrestricted Tool Parameter Schemas
findings.owasp_ref: MCP-004: Command Injection via Tool Parameters
findings.remediation: Add explicit 'type', 'enum', 'pattern', or 'format' constraints to every tool parameter schema. Use the most restrictive constraint applicable (enum > pattern > type).

findings.title: Tool Poisoning Risk — Tools Registered Without Descriptions
findings.remediation: Every registered tool must have a clear, concise description that states exactly what it does and what inputs it expects. Reject tools/list responses that omit descriptions.
